question: Which of the following sermons of Gautama Buddha known as Fire Sermon?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Adittapariyaya Sutta**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Adittapariyaya Sutta** is known as the Fire Sermon given by Gautama Buddha.
 
• The Fire Sermon is one of the most famous discourses of Buddha, delivered to a group of thousand bhikkhus.
 
• In this sermon, Buddha uses the metaphor of fire to explain the nature of human suffering and the path to liberation.
 
• The sermon emphasizes detachment from the senses and the impermanent nature of all things.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Brahmajala Sutra** is a discourse on ethical precepts and moral conduct.
 
• The **Anatta-lakkhana Sutta** is the discourse on the characteristic of non-self.
 
• The **Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta** is the first sermon of the Buddha, setting in motion the Wheel of Dharma.
 
• Gautama Buddha's teachings revolve around the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path as a means to attain Nirvana.
 
• Buddha's discourses are compiled in the Sutta Pitaka, one of the three main divisions of the Pali Canon.
